gate_reading.terminal_headroom: residual above eps_abs=0.05 in all four runs (min 0.0772)

model: dense GRU H=64, input 6, head 32; Adam 3e-3; batch 128
reading: Budget doubling decides the R2 compressibility question. From 1600 to 6400 updates the control's KL is flat (F seeds 0.070->0.080 and 0.157->0.137; X 0.081->0.081 and 0.076->0.077; all |delta| <= 0.010), so the residual is a genuine plateau, not undertraining. Residuals 0.077-0.137 nats sit above the 0.05 nat headroom scale => the theta posterior is NOT fully compressible into a 64-dimensional state and terminal headroom exists. Caveat: the analytic cost of forcing a two-group belief state is only 0.063 nat, and the dense control's X residual (0.081/0.077) is at or above that floor, so the headroom is not purely organisation-shaped -- a better model of any kind could capture part of it, and the interaction must be read as a learnability effect.
